title: The BTS Effect: K-Pop Superstars Drive Major Economic Growth in US Cities
subtitle: As the world-famous group returns to North America, local businesses and tourism sectors see a massive financial boost.

summary.en: The K-pop group BTS has returned to the United States for a world tour after a four-year break. Their arrival is creating a significant economic boost in cities like New York and New Jersey. Local businesses are partnering with the group's label, HYBE, to offer special experiences for fans. Experts suggest that the economic impact of these concerts may match or even exceed major global sporting events. This trend highlights how K-pop acts as a powerful gateway for broader interest in Korean culture and products.
summary.zh: 韓國流行音樂團體防彈少年團在歷經四年空窗期後，重返美國展開世界巡演。他們的到來為紐約與紐澤西等城市帶來顯著的經濟成長。在地商家正與該團體的經紀公司 HYBE 合作，為粉絲提供特別體驗。專家認為，這些演唱會的經濟影響力可能追平甚至超越全球大型體育賽事。此趨勢凸顯了韓國流行音樂如何成為引發大眾對韓國文化與產品廣泛興趣的強大媒介。

paragraphs.en: The K-pop supergroup BTS is back on the road, and their return to North America is creating a wave of economic growth across the United States. Following a four-year break from touring, the group is currently performing 14 shows across six American cities. This tour follows the successful release of their sixth album, Arirang, which has encouraged fans to travel and spend money in the cities where the band performs.
paragraphs.zh: 韓國流行音樂超級團體防彈少年團（BTS）重返巡演之路，他們回歸北美市場正為全美各地帶來一波經濟成長。在歷經四年的巡演空窗期後，該團體目前正在美國六座城市舉辦十四場演出。此次巡演緊接在他們第六張專輯《阿里郎》（Arirang）成功發行之後，這張專輯鼓勵了粉絲前往演出城市旅遊並進行消費。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the financial impact of these concerts is significant. In Las Vegas, for example, four sold-out shows in May generated an estimated $340 million in economic activity. This money was spent not only at large hotels on the famous strip but also at small local businesses, such as cafes in Chinatown. Experts now believe that the spending habits of BTS fans, often called the “Army,” are comparable to those seen at major international events like the World Cup.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，這些演唱會帶來的財務影響相當顯著。以拉斯維加斯為例，五月份四場門票售罄的演出估計創造了三億四千萬美元的經濟效益。這些資金不僅流向了賭城大道上的大型飯店，也挹注了唐人街咖啡館等小型在地商家。專家目前認為，被稱為「阿米」（Army）的防彈少年團粉絲，其消費習慣已可與世界盃等大型國際賽事相提並論。

paragraphs.en: Michael Mariano, who leads economic development at Tourism Economics, noted that the group’s return will likely match or even exceed the economic impact of the recent FIFA World Cup final. This is good news for HYBE, the group’s label, which recently reported record-high revenue of $993 million for the past quarter. The label has worked hard to turn these concerts into a larger experience through a project called “BTS The City – Arirang.”
paragraphs.zh: 旅遊經濟學公司（Tourism Economics）負責經濟發展的麥可·馬里亞諾（Michael Mariano）指出，該團體的回歸所帶來的經濟影響，極有可能追平甚至超越近期舉辦的國際足總世界盃（FIFA World Cup）決賽。這對防彈少年團的經紀公司 HYBE 來說是個好消息，該公司近期公布上一季營收創下九億九千三百萬美元的歷史新高。經紀公司透過名為「BTS The City – Arirang」的計畫，致力於將這些演唱會轉化為更宏大的體驗。

paragraphs.en: This project connects the concerts to local businesses and cultural centers. In New York and New Jersey, fans can follow a special map that highlights local landmarks, restaurants, and activities. For instance, the Korean Cultural Center New York is acting as a main hub for fans. Visitors with reservations can try Korean beauty products, sample desserts from the bakery chain Tous les Jours, and customize their “Army bombs,” which are the light sticks fans carry during performances. Bora Yoon, a visual arts manager at the center, explained that K-pop serves as a gateway. She noted that it helps people learn the Korean language and discover other parts of the culture, such as technology, food, and tourism.
paragraphs.zh: 此計畫將演唱會與在地商家及文化中心連結起來。在紐約與紐澤西，粉絲可以參考一份特別地圖，上面標註了在地地標、餐廳與各類活動。例如，紐約韓國文化中心（Korean Cultural Center New York）便成為粉絲的主要聚集地。持有預約的訪客可以體驗韓國美妝產品、品嚐多樂之日（Tous les Jours）連鎖烘焙坊的甜點，並客製化他們在演出時攜帶的應援棒「阿米棒」。該中心的視覺藝術經理尹寶拉（Bora Yoon）解釋，韓國流行音樂扮演了入門磚的角色。她指出，這有助於人們學習韓語，並進一步探索韓國文化的其他面向，例如科技、飲食與觀光。

paragraphs.en: Digital art is also playing a large role in this economic boom. The Arte Museum is hosting a special exhibit that uses music and digital art to celebrate the group. Sang Jin Lee, a vice-president at the company that owns the museum, said they expect high demand for the exhibit. He explained that the goal is to share Korean heritage and modern digital art through the music of BTS, using the traditional folk song “Arirang” as a central theme. The museum aims to immerse fans in an experience that engages all five senses.
paragraphs.zh: 數位藝術也在這波經濟熱潮中扮演重要角色。藝術博物館（Arte Museum）正舉辦一場特別展覽，透過音樂與數位藝術來頌揚該團體。該博物館所屬公司的副總裁李尚進（Sang Jin Lee，音譯）表示，他們預期展覽將有高度需求。他解釋，目標是透過防彈少年團的音樂，以傳統民謠《阿里郎》為核心主題，分享韓國文化遺產與現代數位藝術。博物館旨在讓粉絲沉浸在能調動五感的體驗之中。

paragraphs.en: Local food businesses are also finding creative ways to welcome fans. New Wonjo, a well-known Korean barbecue restaurant in New York, has created a special menu for the tour. Instead of just using the band’s name to sell food, the restaurant developed dishes like kimchi fried rice and black bean noodles based on the foods the band members miss while traveling. Jacob Baik, the art director at New Wonjo, said the menu was created with care. He hopes that guests who visit because of the “BTS The City” project will leave with a genuine interest in Korean food and culture.
paragraphs.zh: 在地餐飲業者也正以創意方式歡迎粉絲。紐約知名的韓國烤肉餐廳「New Wonjo」為此次巡演設計了特別菜單。餐廳並非僅僅利用團體名氣來銷售餐點，而是開發了如泡菜炒飯與炸醬麵等料理，這些都是團員在巡演期間懷念的家鄉味。New Wonjo 的藝術總監雅各·白（Jacob Baik，音譯）表示，這份菜單是精心設計的。他希望因為「BTS The City」計畫而造訪的賓客，在離開時能對韓國飲食與文化產生真正的興趣。

paragraphs.en: Other businesses are also joining in. A pop-up shop called Seoul Bingsu is offering a popular South Korean shaved ice dessert to concertgoers. These efforts show how a single music tour can support many different types of businesses, from large museums to small family-owned restaurants. As the tour continues through August and September, cities across the United States are preparing for the continued influx of fans.
paragraphs.zh: 其他商家也紛紛加入行列。一家名為「Seoul Bingsu」的快閃店正為演唱會觀眾提供受歡迎的南韓刨冰甜點。這些努力顯示出一場音樂巡演如何能支持從大型博物館到小型家庭式餐廳等各類商家。隨著巡演在八月與九月持續進行，全美各地的城市正為迎接源源不絕的粉絲做好準備。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the success of this tour suggests that the influence of K-pop on the US economy will remain strong. By linking music with local culture and tourism, HYBE and its partners have created a model that brings fans closer to the artists while providing a major boost to local economies. Whether through food, art, or language, the “BTS effect” is proving to be a lasting force that goes far beyond the concert stage.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，此次巡演的成功顯示韓國流行音樂對美國經濟的影響力將持續強勁。透過將音樂與在地文化及觀光結合，HYBE 及其合作夥伴建立了一種模式，在為粉絲拉近與偶像距離的同時，也為在地經濟提供了強大的助力。無論是透過飲食、藝術還是語言，「防彈效應」正證明其影響力深遠，遠遠超越了演唱會舞台本身。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Traveling again, especially for a series of performances or a tour.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 重新開始巡迴演出、再次上路。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思容易被誤解為「回到馬路上」，這裡指藝人恢復巡演。文中：The K-pop supergroup BTS is back on the road, and their return to North America is creating a wave of economic growth across the United States.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A central point or place where a lot of activity happens.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常指交通樞紐，這裡指活動的聚集中心。文中：For instance, the Korean Cultural Center New York is acting as a main hub for fans.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Something that provides a way to enter or experience a new field or culture.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面為「門道」，這裡比喻為接觸新事物的入口。文中：Bora Yoon, a visual arts manager at the center, explained that K-pop serves as a gateway.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A person or thing that has a strong influence or effect.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見為「武力」或「強迫」，這裡指具有影響的人事物。文中：Whether through food, art, or language, the “BTS effect” is proving to be a lasting force that goes far beyond the concert stage.

quiz.question: What specific activity can fans engage in at the Korean Cultural Center New York as part of the 'BTS The City' project?

options.A: They can watch a live performance by the band members.
options.B: They can personalize the light sticks they use during concerts.
options.C: They can purchase tickets for the upcoming World Cup events.
options.D: They can attend a lecture on the history of the song 'Arirang'.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，粉絲可以在紐約的韓國文化中心自訂（customize）他們的「Army bombs」，也就是演唱會使用的應援棒。選項 A 錯誤，文中未提到成員現場表演；選項 C 與文章提到的 World Cup 經濟影響力比較無關；選項 D 雖然提到了「Arirang」是主題，但文中並未提到有關於該歌曲的歷史講座。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might the 'BTS The City' project be considered a successful business model?

options.A: It forces fans to spend money only at large, corporate-owned hotels.
options.B: It relies entirely on digital art to attract tourists to major cities.
options.C: It creates a multi-layered experience that integrates music, local culture, and commerce.
options.D: It ensures that local businesses do not have to change their menus or services.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章最後一段與第四段，該計畫透過將音樂與當地文化、美食及旅遊結合，成功創造了讓粉絲更貼近藝人的體驗，同時帶動了不同規模企業的經濟。選項 A 錯誤，文中提到包含小型當地企業；選項 B 錯誤，數位藝術只是其中一部分，並非全部；選項 D 錯誤，文中明確提到餐廳為了迎接粉絲而開發了特別菜單。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'gateway' mean in the context of K-pop's role?

options.A: A physical entrance to a building or stadium.
options.B: A technological barrier that prevents people from accessing content.
options.C: A point of entry or introduction to a broader subject or culture.
options.D: A financial tool used to process payments for concert tickets.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文中提到 K-pop 作為一個「gateway」，能幫助人們學習韓語並進一步探索韓國的飲食、科技與旅遊，因此這裡的 gateway 指的是通往更廣泛文化領域的入門或橋樑。選項 A 是字面意思，但在文中不適用；選項 B 與文中正面影響的語意相反；選項 D 與金融交易無關。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding BTS's recent tour?

options.A: The tour is primarily focused on breaking international music sales records.
options.B: The tour has created a significant and diverse economic impact by connecting music with local cultural experiences.
options.C: The tour has caused major traffic and logistical problems for American cities.
options.D: The tour is mainly intended to promote the Korean Cultural Center's beauty products.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。全文旨在探討 BTS 的巡演如何透過「BTS The City」計畫，將音樂影響力轉化為對美國各地（從大型企業到小型餐廳）的實質經濟貢獻。選項 A 雖然提到專輯，但非文章主旨；選項 C 文章未提及；選項 D 僅是文中提到的一個細節活動，並非整篇文章的核心目的。
